The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Exclusive License and Product Development Agreement’. Its operative core centers on Section 2, which grants an exclusive right and license to products, regulatory dossiers, and background intellectual property for commercialization in a defined territory. The financial structure relies on upfront licensing fees, sales-based milestones, and running royalties, which are hallmark features of IP/license agreements. Although it contains regulatory development and manufacturing covenants, these serve as conditions and obligations ancillary to the primary grant of an exclusive license, firmly categorizing it under the license family.

Exhibit 4 explicitly references the parent contract as a ‘Specialty Distributor Purchase and Service Agreement,’ confirming the substantive family.

The document is explicitly titled ‘MANUFACTURING, DESIGN AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses overwhelmingly govern the production, pricing, tooling, delivery, inventory, and FDA regulatory compliance of manufactured medical devices. Under the hybrid agreement rules, the operative core of manufacturing production and supply commitments dictates the ‘manufacturing’ classification.

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement.’ While the title references licensing and marketing, the operative clauses predominantly establish EKR as the exclusive distributor, detail sub-distributor appointments, define net sales and royalty calculations based on resale, and govern territorial sales, warehousing, and supply chain logistics. Per the hybrid agreement rules, the substantive commercial distribution and resale machinery controls the classification over the ancillary license and marketing provisions.

While marketing activities are included, the substantive commercial machinery focuses on resale and distribution, making ‘reseller’ the best fit under the contract subtypes.

The operative clauses (Sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8) are dominated by manufacturing obligations: purchase orders for products to be manufactured by the Subcontractor, pricing based on manufacturing costs, delivery terms (FOB), warranties for nonconforming products, and termination of manufacturing orders. While it contains design/engineering services and a joint marketing provision (Section 9), the core substantive agreement is the manufacturing of goods. Under Rule 24 (‘Outsourcing Title Wins’), an agreement titled ‘Manufacturing… Agreement’ where the function is manufacturing is classified as manufacturing. It is not outsourcing because the title explicitly names manufacturing and the relationship is a direct manufacturer-subcontractor supply chain rather than a business process outsourcing arrangement.

13. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is an ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement’. It contains operative clauses for licensing (Section 2.2), distribution (Section 2.1 appointing EKR as exclusive distributor), and marketing (Section 4.6). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), the agreement’s core obligations regarding purchase, resale, order terms, and sales force deployment fall under the distributor family. While it includes marketing and license elements, the commercial machinery of distribution and resale is central to the agreement’s structure and purpose.

14. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Section 1 and Section 2) contain standard non-disclosure obligations and covenants not to compete or solicit, which fall squarely under the ‘non_compete_no_solicit’ subtype. Although it is an appendix within a larger filing context, the substantive form is a restrictive covenant agreement.

15. SteelVaultCorp_20081224_10-K_EX-10.16_3074935_EX-10.16_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’ and the Recitals state it constitutes a ‘marketing agreement’. The operative clauses grant the Marketing Affiliate permission to display materials and market services via direct mail, telemarketing, and web links. Under Rule 26 (‘MARKETING TITLE WINS’), an agreement titled with ‘Marketing’ where the core activity is promotion/placement of products is classified as marketing, even if it contains affiliate/referral elements. It is not an ‘affiliate’ subtype because the primary function described is active marketing/solicitation rather than passive referral tracking, and the title dictates the classification.

16. CybergyHoldingsInc_20140520_10-Q_EX-10.27_8605784_EX-10.27_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses grant the Marketing Affiliate (MA) the right to ‘advertise, market and sell’ the Company’s Technology. While it involves resale, the agreement explicitly states that MA is not required to follow a marketing plan prescribed by the Company and focuses on marketing activities, sales quotas, and promotional support. Per Rule 26 (‘MARKETING TITLE WINS’), an agreement titled ‘Marketing… Agreement’ where the core is promotion/placement of products is classified as marketing, even if it contains agency or distributor-like machinery. It is not a pure distributor agreement because the primary obligation described is marketing/selling via affiliate channels rather than independent distribution rights, and the title controls.

While it contains a license grant (Section II) and supply terms (Section IV), the operative core of the agreement places significant obligations on SCIEN to execute a Business Plan, manage logistics, hold inventory, provide sales forecasts, and actively promote/distribute the product in the Territory. The commercial machinery of purchase, resale, and distribution rights dominates the substantive obligations. Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when development plans are absent but commercial/resale terms are present, the distributor family is the best fit. The confidence is capped at 0.85 because the agreement is a hybrid involving both supply and licensing elements.

12. Zounds Hearing, Inc. - MANUFACTURING DESIGN MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted manufacturing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘MANUFACTURING, DESIGN AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’. While it contains marketing provisions (Section 9), the substantive operative core of the agreement revolves around the manufacturing of hearing aids by the Subcontractor for the Manufacturer. Key clauses include purchase orders for manufactured goods (Section 3), product pricing based on manufacturing costs (Section 3.3), engineering and design services related to production (Section 3.7), tooling and NRE charges (Section 3.8), delivery terms (Section 4), and regulatory compliance for medical device manufacturing (Section 14). The marketing component is secondary and described as a separate joint arrangement. Under Rule 26 (‘MARKETING TITLE WINS’), one might consider marketing, but Rule 26 explicitly carves out agreements where the title’s PRIMARY family is another specific operational service family like manufacturing. Furthermore, Rule 24 establishes that outsourcing titles win, but this is a direct manufacturing supply relationship rather than a business-process outsourcing arrangement. The dominant economic activity and legal obligations are manufacturing and supply of goods, fitting the ‘manufacturing’ subtype.

13. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is an ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement’. It contains operative clauses for licensing (Section 2.2), marketing (Section 4.6), and distribution (Section 2.1). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when the title names multiple families, we weigh the operative clauses. The agreement appoints EKR as the ‘exclusive distributor’ with rights to sell, distribute, warehouse, and appoint sub-distributors, and includes standard supply chain mechanics (purchase obligations, net sales definitions, royalties on sales). While it includes marketing and IP license elements, these are ancillary to the core commercial relationship of distributing and selling the product. Therefore, ‘distributor’ is the best fit among the specific families.

14. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. Its operative clauses (Sections 1 and 2) establish confidentiality obligations and covenants not to compete or solicit customers/employees. While it exists within a franchise context, the substantive agreement between the Franchisee and its personnel is a restrictive covenant agreement, fitting the non_compete_no_solicit subtype.

15. EhaveInc_20190515_20-F_EX-4.44_11678816_EX-4.44_License Agreement_ Reseller Agreement — expected reseller vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is titled ‘LICENSE AND RESELLER AGREEMENT’. It contains both a license grant (Section 2(b)) and an exclusive appointment for CHT to resell the solution (Section 2(a)). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when an agreement combines license and distribution/resale elements, the operative core determines the subtype. The agreement explicitly appoints CHT as a ‘reseller’ with exclusive rights to sell/sub-license in a specific field of use, includes royalty structures based on sales, audit rights for revenue verification, and marketing obligations typical of a distribution channel. While it involves software licensing, the commercial mechanism is resale/distribution. Therefore, it fits the ‘distributor’ family better than ‘license’ or ‘other’. Confidence is slightly lowered (0.85) due to the hybrid nature (License + Reseller), but the reseller machinery is dominant.

16. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses establish a joint venture structure for specific activities (AMR market development). Section 4.1 states: ‘The parties will be joint venturers only as to those activities that they jointly undertake…’. The agreement details joint ownership of IP developed during the collaboration (Section 3.1.1), shared marketing rights, and profit/loss sharing mechanisms typical of a joint venture. While the title says ‘Affiliate’, Rule 27 defines ‘affiliate’ contracts as those with referral/commission machinery (links, referral fees). This contract lacks that machinery and instead creates a formal JV entity-like relationship for product development and sales. Therefore, it falls under the ‘joint_venture’ family based on its substantive legal effect, consistent with the instruction to classify by substantive form rather than title when the title is misleading or generic.

However, looking at the specific list, ‘reseller’ is also an option. Rule 26 states ‘MARKETING TITLE WINS’ but doesn’t apply here. Rule 9 says to weigh operative clauses. The agreement grants a license to sub-license. It also has a reseller appointment. In many corpora, ‘License and Reseller’ is classified as License if the IP transfer/use is central, or Distributor/Reseller if the sales channel is central. Here, the ‘Grant by Ehave’ is a license to sub-license. The ‘Appointment’ is to act as a reseller. Given the explicit title ‘LICENSE AND RESELLER’, and the fact that ‘reseller’ is a valid subtype key, I need to decide between license and reseller. The prompt lists ‘reseller’ as ‘Reseller Agreement — Reseller and value-added distribution’. It lists ‘license’ as ‘License Agreement — Licensing of technology, content, or IP’. The document grants a license to use and sub-license the software. This is fundamentally a license agreement that includes reseller rights. Often, these are filed under License. Let’s look at Rule 13: Maintenance wins if titled so. Not applicable. Rule 22: IP Agreement wins if titled so. Not applicable. Between License and Reseller: The primary obligation is the provision of the software via license. The reseller part is the commercial mechanism. I will classify as ‘license’ because the grant of rights to the underlying IP is the foundational element enabling the resale.

19. ParatekPharmaceuticalsInc_20170505_10-KA_EX-10.29_10323872_EX-10.29_Outsourcing Agreement — expected outsourcing vs predicted manufacturing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Outsourcing Agreement’ in the header, but the operative clauses and recitals define the core obligation as the Supplier’s performance of ‘Manufacturing Services’ for the Product (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients). Specifically, Recital C states the Supplier is engaged in ‘contracted process development, Manufacturing and supply services,’ and Article 3 is titled ‘Supply of Product’ with Section 3.2 detailing ‘Manufacturing Services.’ Under Rule 24 (‘OUTSOURCING TITLE WINS’), an agreement titled ‘Outsourcing Agreement’ where the outsourced function is manufacturing is classified as ‘manufacturing’ because the title names the family and the operative machinery is manufacturing production. The agreement governs the physical production, quality control, and supply of goods, fitting the manufacturing family.

20. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. Its operative clauses establish confidentiality obligations and restrictive covenants (non-compete, non-solicitation of customers/employees) between a franchisee and its personnel. While it references a Franchise Agreement, this document itself is the restrictive covenant agreement, fitting the ‘non_compete_no_solicit’ subtype.

21. PlayboyEnterprisesInc_20090220_10-QA_EX-10.2_4091580_EX-10.2_Content License Agreement_ Marketing Agreement_ … — expected license vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘CONTENT LICENSE, MARKETING AND SALES AGREEMENT’. Per Rule 30 (Marketing Title Wins — Strengthened), when the title names marketing alongside other families like license or sales/distributor, the agreement is classified as marketing if it contains marketing/promotion obligations. The operative clauses extensively detail EFS’s obligations to market and promote the Playboy Commerce Business via catalogs and websites (Sections 1.1(a), 4.1-4.6), including specific advertising budgets and SEO efforts. While it includes a content license grant and sales/fulfillment mechanics, the title and core operational focus on brand promotion and channel management align with the marketing family under the corpus convention.

**22. LejuHoldingsLtd_20140121_DRS (on F-1)_EX-10.26_8473102_EX-10.26_Content License Agreement2** — expected license vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: other_fallback

The document is a ‘Mutual Termination Agreement’ between two parties to end a prior license agreement. While it is a formal contract, the specific subtype ‘termination’ or ‘mutual release’ is not among the listed valid contract subtypes (e.g., license, distributor, service). It does not fit the substantive machinery of any other specific family like manufacturing, marketing, or joint venture. Therefore, per rule 8, it falls under ‘other’.

23. ScansourceInc_20190822_10-K_EX-10.38_11793958_EX-10.38_Distributor Agreement2 — expected distributor vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Software License Agreement’ and its primary operative clause grants a nonexclusive, nontransferable license to use software. It contains standard license restrictions (no reverse engineering, no modification) and IP protection clauses. While it includes warranty and liability disclaimers typical of commercial contracts, the substantive legal relationship defined is a software license.

24. RitterPharmaceuticalsInc_20200313_S-4A_EX-10.54_12055220_EX-10.54_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘DISTRIBUTION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. While it contains significant development machinery (Development Plan, milestones, R&D subcommittee, financing for development), Rule 9 requires weighing the operative clauses. The agreement’s core commercial structure is an exclusive distribution appointment where Sekisui purchases and resells Qualigen’s products, including detailed supply terms, purchase orders, pricing/margin sharing based on resale, and inventory management. The development component serves as a funding mechanism tied to the distribution relationship rather than a standalone R&D collaboration. Therefore, the commercial distributor family is the primary fit. Confidence is capped at 0.85 due to the hybrid nature of the title and the substantial presence of development provisions.

25. RevolutionMedicinesInc_20200117_S-1_EX-10.1_11948417_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

It establishes a joint research and development program governed by specific committees (JSC, JRDC, JCC) and includes provisions for shared IP, cost sharing, and commercialization rights. This fits the definition of a Collaboration Agreement. While it contains development machinery, Rule 21 specifies that agreements with titles naming ‘Collaborative… Development’ are classified as collaboration because the governance structure defines the family.

26. LiquidmetalTechnologiesInc_20200205_8-K_EX-10.1_11968198_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ and establishes a multi-faceted relationship between Liquidmetal and Eutectix. While it contains significant license grants (Section 2.4) and manufacturing/supply obligations (Section 3), the operative core includes explicit collaboration machinery: Section 6.3 mandates annual meetings to ‘collaborate on advancements,’ Section 8 governs joint ownership of newly developed IP (‘New Amorphous Alloy Technology’), and the Recitals express a desire to ‘further collaborate.’ Under Rule 9 and Rule 21, when an agreement combines development/collaboration governance (joint IP ownership, R&D cooperation) with other elements, the collaborative/development nature prevails over pure licensing or supply. Between ‘development’ and ‘collaboration’, the title ‘Business Development Agreement’ and the mutual, ongoing cooperative structure (joint steering via meetings, shared IP rights) align best with the ‘collaboration’ family (R&D and cooperation collaborations), distinct from a unilateral ‘development’ service agreement.

27. EtonPharmaceuticalsInc_20191114_10-Q_EX-10.1_11893941_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

While it contains development obligations (Section 3), Rule 19 states that when an agreement combines development machinery with license grants for developed IP, the license grant is the delivery mechanism, but the title and core commercial structure (exclusive rights to market/sell in exchange for royalties/milestones) align with a License Agreement. The ‘Product Development’ aspect refers to the regulatory development required to enable the licensed product’s commercialization, which is standard in pharma licensing deals. The primary legal relationship is the licensing of IP rights.

28. EmeraldHealthBioceuticalsInc_20200218_1-A_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_11987205_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted consulting (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Consulting and Product Development Agreement’ but the operative clauses (Article 2) define Dr. Murray’s role as providing ‘ongoing services,’ ‘guidance,’ ‘advice,’ and ‘general assistance’ in a capacity consistent with an independent contractor or consultant. Article 9 explicitly states the parties are acting as ‘independent contractors.’ While product development is mentioned, it is framed as the subject of the consulting advice rather than a standalone development obligation with milestones or joint R&D governance typical of a ‘development’ agreement. The core legal relationship is the provision of professional consulting services.

29. ElPolloLocoHoldingsInc_20200306_10-K_EX-10.16_12041700_EX-10.16_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted franchise (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘EL POLLO LOCO® FRANCHISE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses grant the Developer rights to establish and operate franchised restaurants under the Franchisor’s system, require the execution of individual Franchise Agreements for each site, and reference the Franchise Disclosure Document. While it contains development milestones (a ‘development’ feature), Rule 21 specifically states that a ‘Franchise Development Agreement’ or similar structure where the core is granting franchise rights for developed units is classified as ‘franchise’, not ‘development’. The agreement serves as the master framework for future franchise relationships.

30. ArcaUsTreasuryFund_20200207_N-2_EX-99.K5_11971930_EX-99.K5_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘FORM OF BLOCKCHAIN ADMINISTRATION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ between a Fund and a Blockchain Administrator. The operative clauses (Section 1) define the Administrator’s role as an independent contractor providing ‘development and administrative services,’ including coding, smart contract maintenance, and general fund administration (record keeping, reporting, liaison with agents). While it contains development elements, the broader scope of administrative duties and the nature of the relationship (hiring a service provider for ongoing operational support rather than a specific R&D milestone project) aligns best with a Service Agreement. It is not a license, distribution, or joint venture. The ‘development’ aspect is part of the service delivery.

31. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily focus on the Endorser (Arnold Schwarzenegger) lending his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm’s products (Section 2, Section 3). It includes standard endorsement machinery such as personal appearances, approval of advertising materials, FTC compliance affidavits, exclusivity/non-competition regarding competing dietary supplements, and compensation via royalties and stock for these endorsement services. While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, the core substantive obligation is the celebrity endorsement.

32. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses define a joint development and commercialization relationship for AMR products. Section 3 details joint development efforts, joint ownership of IP, coordinated marketing/sales roles, and profit-sharing mechanisms. Section 4.1 explicitly states the parties are ‘joint venturers’ only for these specific activities. Under Rule 21 (‘Development Versus Collaboration…’), a collaborative agreement with joint R&D/development machinery (joint steering, shared IP, joint product development) is classified as collaboration. The ‘affiliate’ title refers to the business relationship structure rather than an affiliate/referral program (Rule 27), and the core obligations are collaborative development and commercialization.

Specifically, Recital C states the Supplier is engaged in ‘contracted process development, Manufacturing and supply services,’ and Article 3 is titled ‘Supply of Product’ with Section 3.2 detailing ‘Manufacturing Services.’ Under Rule 24 (‘OUTSOURCING TITLE WINS’), an agreement titled ‘Outsourcing Agreement’ where the outsourced function is manufacturing is classified as ‘manufacturing’ because the title names the family and the operative machinery is manufacturing production. The document does not fit ‘supply’ (which implies generic goods) or ‘service’ (generic professional services) as precisely as it fits the specific manufacturing outsourcing context governed by cGMP and quality agreements typical of pharma manufacturing.

17. AudibleInc_20001113_10-Q_EX-10.32_2599586_EX-10.32_Co-Branding Agreement_ Marketing Agreement_ Investment Dis… — expected marketing vs predicted co_branding (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘CO-BRANDING, MARKETING AND DISTRIBUTION AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses establish a co-branded presence on the ACSI (Amazon) site for Audible’s products, involving shared branding, joint press releases, and integrated site functionality. Under Rule 6 and Rule 26, when the title names a specific family like ‘Co-Branding’, it takes precedence. The agreement fits the definition of a Co-Branding Agreement where two parties combine their brands/products in a joint offering.

18. ArtaraTherapeuticsInc_20200110_8-K_EX-10.5_11943350_EX-10.5_License Agreement — expected license vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is titled ‘Sponsored Research and License Agreement’. It contains substantive development machinery: a defined ‘Project’ with specific phases (feasibility analysis, data compilation, BLA filing), milestone payments tied to regulatory approval, and joint IP ownership provisions for inventions arising from the project. Per Rule 19 and Rule 21, when an agreement combines license grants with development machinery (plans, milestones, R&D/clinical trials), it is classified as ‘development’. The title explicitly names ‘Research’ (synonymous with development in this context) and ‘License’, but the operative core driving the commercial relationship is the sponsored research/development of the product TARA-002.

19. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. Its operative clauses (Section 1: Confidential Information; Section 2: Covenants Not to Compete) establish restrictive covenants regarding confidentiality, non-competition, and non-solicitation. Although it is an appendix within a regulatory filing (10-12G), the substantive form is a contract containing non-compete/no-solicit provisions.

**20. LejuHoldingsLtd_20140121_DRS (on F-1)_EX-10.26_8473102_EX-10.26_Content License Agreement2** — expected license vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: other_fallback

The document is explicitly titled ‘MUTUAL TERMINATION AGREEMENT’ and contains operative clauses for terminating a prior agreement (‘Original Agreement’). While it is a formal contract between parties, the specific subtype ‘termination’ or ‘mutual termination’ is not among the valid contract subgroups listed in the schema (e.g., license, distributor, service). It does not fit into other specific families like ‘agency’ or ‘consulting’. Therefore, per Rule 8, it falls under ‘other’ as it genuinely matches none of the listed families.

21. ScansourceInc_20190822_10-K_EX-10.38_11793958_EX-10.38_Distributor Agreement2 — expected distributor vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Software License Agreement’ and its primary operative clause grants a nonexclusive, nontransferable license to use software. It contains standard license terms regarding scope of use, restrictions (no reverse engineering), IP ownership retention, and warranty disclaimers specific to licensed software. It does not contain significant maintenance, development, or hosting obligations that would trigger the exceptions in rules 13, 14, or 19.

22. RitterPharmaceuticalsInc_20200313_S-4A_EX-10.54_12055220_EX-10.54_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘DISTRIBUTION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. It contains substantial operative machinery for both distribution (exclusive appointment, purchase/resale obligations, supply terms, pricing/margin sharing) and development (development plan, milestones, financing payments for R&D). Per Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), we weigh the operative clauses. While there is a development component, the agreement’s core commercial structure is the exclusive distribution of products, including detailed provisions on supply, orders, inventory, marketing claims, and margin splits. The development aspect serves to secure future product lines for the distributor. Therefore, it fits the ‘distributor’ family best. Confidence is capped at 0.85 due to the significant hybrid nature with development elements.

23. RevolutionMedicinesInc_20200117_S-1_EX-10.1_11948417_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH, DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION AGREEMENT’. It establishes a joint research program governed by a Joint Steering Committee (JSC) and other joint committees, with shared governance and IP provisions typical of biopharmaceutical collaborations. Per Rule 21, agreements with this title and development machinery are classified as ‘collaboration’ rather than ‘development’, as the collaboration governance structure defines the family.

24. EtonPharmaceuticalsInc_20191114_10-Q_EX-10.1_11893941_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is explicitly titled ‘EXCLUSIVE LICENSE AND PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. It contains a primary operative clause (Section 2.1) granting an exclusive license to intellectual property and products. While it includes development obligations (Section 3), the agreement’s core structure and title prioritize the license grant. Under Rule 31 (License-Primary Title Wins), a title naming license as the primary family classifies the document as a license, even when co-named with other families like development or marketing, unless specific hybrid rules (like Development Preference in Rule 10/19) override it. However, Rule 19 states development wins over license only when there is a ‘development plan, milestones or trial timelines… joint steering/R&D committee’. Here, the development section is largely regulatory filing responsibility (‘ANDA Litigation’, ‘Dossiers’) rather than active R&D/clinical development milestones typical of a pure Development Agreement. Furthermore, Rule 31 specifically carves out that a ‘Content License Agreement’ (and by extension, a License-titled agreement) stays license. The dominant legal mechanism is the transfer of IP rights via license for commercialization.

25. EmeraldHealthBioceuticalsInc_20200218_1-A_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_11987205_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted consulting (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Consulting and Product Development Agreement’ but the operative clauses (Article 2) define Dr. Murray’s role as providing ‘guidance’, ‘advice’, ‘general assistance’, and acting as an ‘advocate’. These are classic consulting services rather than a commitment to deliver specific developed products or milestones typical of a development agreement. The agreement explicitly states in Article 9(4) that parties are independent contractors. While it involves product development context, the core obligation is advisory/consulting. Rule 10 suggests preferring development if there is a development plan/milestones, but here the obligations are ongoing services (‘ongoing services’, ‘provide guidance’) without specific technical milestones or R&D committee structures typical of pure development agreements. It fits best under Consulting.

26. ElPolloLocoHoldingsInc_20200306_10-K_EX-10.16_12041700_EX-10.16_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted franchise (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘EL POLLO LOCO® FRANCHISE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. It establishes a relationship between a Franchisor (El Pollo Loco) and a Developer to open multiple restaurants under the franchise system. The operative clauses grant development rights contingent upon executing individual Franchise Agreements, reference the Franchise Disclosure Document, and include standard franchise provisions like proprietary rights, operations manuals, and non-compete covenants specific to the franchise system. Rule 21 specifically states that a ‘Franchise Development Agreement’ is classified as franchise, not development.

27. ArcaUsTreasuryFund_20200207_N-2_EX-99.K5_11971930_EX-99.K5_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘FORM OF BLOCKCHAIN ADMINISTRATION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ between a Fund and a Blockchain Administrator. The operative clauses (Section 1) define the Administrator’s role as an independent contractor to provide ‘development and administrative services,’ including coding, smart contract maintenance, and general fund administration (record keeping, reporting, relations with agents). While it contains ‘development’ elements (coding ERC-1404 securities), the broader scope of ‘administration’ and the nature of the relationship (hiring a service provider for ongoing operational support rather than a specific R&D milestone project) aligns best with a Service Agreement. It does not fit other specific families like license, hosting, or outsourcing (which typically implies transferring entire business functions) as precisely as the general service category for this hybrid admin/dev role.

28. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily focus on the Endorser (Arnold Schwarzenegger) lending his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm products (Section 2, Section 3). While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, Rule 6 specifically identifies ‘Endorsement Agreement’ as a distinct subgroup for celebrity/influencer deals involving the use of name/likeness for promotion. The core obligation is the endorsement service.

title: llm-entity-extraction — Posit Cloud Portal
text:
How this site is built

Quarto website (site/): rendered to docs/posit/ — the same docs/ tree GitHub Pages serves, so one URL prefix hosts both this portal and the explorer (../index.html). Deployable from Posit Cloud with quarto render + publish; no GitHub Actions anywhere.
Derived, never hand-edited: every page body regenerates from reports/experiment_log.jsonl, MESSAGE_BOARD.md, and MESSAGE_BOARD_DISCUSSION.qmd via site/_pre-render.py on every render; the experiment-log page uses the same renderer (src/experiment_log.py::render_full_log) as reports/experiment_log.md.
Same-sample honesty carries over: headline scores show raw values with sample sizes; significant deltas must come from the paired A/B runs in the log, not from cross-sample eyeballing.







Tip



One URL, two sites. docs/ is served as a whole: the Posit Cloud portal at posit/ and the interactive experiment-log explorer at the root (index.html). They link to each other from the navbar.

title: Agent Kanban Board
text:
The living, shared Kanban canvas for ALL agents (and humans) working in this cross-repository project — the prompt-experiment loop in this repo (llm-entity-extraction) and the pipeline it feeds (llm-mailroom). It is the single place where tasks that still need to be completed, are in progress, are blocked, need to be revisited, or have been finished are tracked — with every card tied to a semantic-version release in CHANGELOG.md and, when critical, to a GitHub issue in the repo where the work lands.
This is a WORKING DOCUMENT, not documentation. It is meant to be modified progressively as work happens. Finished work is never deleted — it moves to the Archive (bottom of this file) so the full audit trail stays intact.

title: Agent Kanban Board
section: How to use this board — the procedures (READ FIRST, every session)
text:
How to use this board — the procedures (READ FIRST, every session)

1. Read before you work
Read this board before starting ANY task — the Kanban table, the discussion log, and the open GitHub issues — for (a) cards/issues already claimed by another agent, (b) cards that cover the work you were about to do, and (c) context posts that affect your work.


2. Scope — one board for both repos
Cards can target either repository. The task summary states the repo or the card names it in the evidence column; llm-mailroom work (pipeline integration, synced prompts/logs) is tracked here with the other cards. Issues for cross-repo work open in the repo where the work lands.


3. Self-assignment (claiming a task)
A task is yours only after you claim it, in this order:

Comment on the GitHub issue (if the card has one — the Issue column) saying you are claiming it, OR post to the Discussion board if the card is board-only. Discussion posts are appended at the TOP of MESSAGE_BOARD_DISCUSSION.qmd (date + agent + card + subject + full post — see the Discussion board section below).
Move the card to in_progress and set Owner to your agent name

today’s date.

Reference the card in your first commit: sorter_v7 (KANBAN-003): ... or MESSAGE BOARD: KANBAN-004 claimed.

Never work silently; never race a claimed card. ONE owner per card — if a card is claimed, build off it (offer help / pick an unclaimed card).


4. Work underway = in_progress, immediately — never backlog
backlog means ZERO work has started: no draft, no diff, no run in flight, no partially landed commit. The moment ANY work exists for a card’s scope — a first working-tree edit, an uncommitted prompt/test/ script draft, a branch, a run that has started — the card MUST be moved to in_progress (Owner set, Updated dated), NOT left in backlog.

Label it before the code, not after. The status move happens when work begins; never when it finishes.
Sanity check every session (and before every commit): if git status (or a branch, or a running eval) shows changes that belong to a card, that card must read in_progress in the table. If a card is found underway-but-labeled-backlog, move it to in_progress at that moment, set Owner to whoever holds the work, and post a dated note in the discussion log. Uncommitted work on the board = an in_progress card.
The table must never lie about reality: a card whose summary says “draft in the working tree” is, by definition, in_progress — update the lane at the same time you write the summary.



5. Work that relates to an existing task MUST update that task
If your work addresses the problem identified in a card — even partially, or from a different angle — you update THAT card: comment on the issue / post to the discussion board, move its status to reflect reality, and extend its summary with what you found. Never create a parallel card for a covered problem and never open a duplicate issue. Only add a NEW card (next free number, new issue if critical) when NO card covers the task.


6. Status moves — when and who








Move
Who
When




backlog → in_progress
anyone (self-assign)
You are actively working it, OR any work exists for it (draft, diff, branch, run started) — Owner set + dated, immediately, never deferred


→ blocked
owner
Stuck — post the blocker in Discussion + on the issue; name what unblocks it (data, keys, decision, card)


blocked → backlog/in_progress
owner
Blocker cleared — post what cleared it


→ in_review
owner
Work done; awaiting validation (tests, A/B, release gate). Link the evidence (run, commit, PR) in the card


in_review → done (Archive)
reviewer/releaser
Validation passed; CHANGELOG entry exists (same-commit rule); issue CLOSED in the same commit


done → backlog (reopen)
anyone
Regression / new data / superseded assumption — Discussion post explains why; issue reopened with the post



A card is not done until every criterion in §7 holds; a synced card’s done and its issue’s closed are the SAME event.


7. Completion — the done & issue-close criteria
A task is COMPLETE — and its dedicated GitHub issue CLOSABLE — only when EVERY requirement holds. All six must be true before you report done:

Work verified — tests pass (network-free suite), the A/B run landed, and/or the release gate (release.py --check) is green. No uncommitted work may remain in the card’s scope — git status is clean for the card’s files (stray diffs mean the card is still in_progress, not done).
CHANGELOG entry exists — the [Unreleased] (or released) entry describing the work lands in the SAME commit that ships it (AGENTS.md same-commit rule). No changelog entry = no done.
Card archived — the card moved to the Archive with: shipped version, commit/tag, key result, and the Owner/Updated timestamp filled.
Discussion closed out — a dated closing entry on the discussion board (result + verdict), newest-at-top, history never edited.
Issue closed in the same commit — for synced cards, gh issue close NNN runs with a closing comment naming the commit and CHANGELOG entry, IN the same commit that archives the card. The card must never sit done with its issue open, nor the issue closed with the card unarchived.
No orphaned scope — anything discovered but NOT delivered (a new confusion cluster, a follow-on arm) spawns its own card + issue BEFORE this card closes; unfinished discovery is not a silent done.

Completion close-out is the LAST action of every task: verify → changelog → archive → discussion post → close issue → report.
Reopen protocol (regression / new data / superseded assumption): move the card back to backlog AND reopen its issue with the Discussion post as the comment — in the same pass.


8. GitHub issue sync (critical / high-priority tasks)
Critical, high-priority, and cross-repo tasks are routed to GitHub issues (label kanban), opened in the repo where the work lands, so agents can open/close them like normal issues while the board remains the source of truth.

Which tasks route to issues: critical / high-priority cards, cross-repo work, anything whose completion must be externally verifiable, and any card the human asks to track as an issue. Board-only cards (small, single-session, low-risk) do NOT need issues.
The card ALWAYS carries the dedicated issue link. Every synced card’s Issue column holds the FULL markdown link to its own dedicated issue — [#NNN](https://github.com/Exios66/<repo>/issues/NNN) — never a bare number, never a link to another card’s issue. One card = one issue.
Order of operations when adding a critical card: open the issue FIRST (in the repo where the work lands), then write its link into the card: gh issue create --title "KANBAN-00N: <task>" --label kanban --body "<card summary + evidence + procedure>".
Cross-reference both ways. The issue body names its KANBAN-00N; the card names its issue link. They must never disagree about status — a lane move on the card is mirrored on the issue (claim → comment, blocked → blocker comment, done → closed).
When a card ships, close its issue in the same commit that archives the card (gh issue close NNN), with a closing comment naming the commit and CHANGELOG entry (see §7.5).
When a card is reopened, reopen its issue with the Discussion post as the comment.
Sync sweep: after any board edit, audit the table — every open card has a link in its Issue column, and every link points at an issue that is OPEN (gh issue list --label kanban), except cards in the Archive, whose issues are CLOSED. A missing link = an unsynced card = not ready for assignment.



9. Commit discipline
Reference cards in commits — MESSAGE BOARD: KANBAN-004 claimed or v24 diagnostic (KANBAN-004): .... A commit that lands a card’s work carries its CHANGELOG entry in the same commit (AGENTS.md rule) and closes its issue.


10. Release sweep
Semantic versioning is the spine: every open card names its target release. When a release ships (scripts/release.py --bump), sweep the board: cards that landed move to the Archive under that version (issues already closed), cards that did not land are re-targeted to the next release. The board and CHANGELOG.md must never disagree about what is done.
